title: Policy decision attribution, weighting, and telemetry notes
content:
Purpose and context:
This doc captures an internal proposal and working notes for how the platform policy evaluation layer should compute decision scores, attribute those decisions to constraint reasons, and emit explainability telemetry that plays nicely with multi-region routing and our control plane. It's deliberately pragmatic — prioritize low-latency inline evals where feasible and fall back to convergent, auditable logs for gold-plated analysis.
content_2:
Goals (high level):
- Deterministic, reproducible decision attribution for debugging and audits.
- Lightweight inline scoring (<= 1ms overhead target for common fast-paths).
- Pluggable constraint language so product teams can author rules without runtime churn.
- Explainability logs that are queryable, privacy-aware, and correlate to request traces across regions.
- Support for multi-region policy variants and eventual consistency without surprising behavior for users.
content_3:
Terminology quick ref:
- Constraint: boolean predicate evaluated against request context (e.g., model_size <= 8B, customer_tier == enterprise).
- Score (raw): numerical weight per constraint or policy branch representing strength of preference.
- Decision score: aggregated numeric value driving routing or action choice.
- Attribution entry: small record capturing which constraints fired and their contribution to the final decision.
- Explainability log: persisted, richer record for later inspection (traces, human-readable reasons, hashes).

Design sketch:
1) Constraint expression language:
  - Use a JSON/YAML-first DSL (existing authors prefer): simple operators (==, !=, in, range, regex) + typed context refs (region, model_family, seq_len_percentile, token_rate).
  - Allow short-circuit flags and precompiled predicates that can be JIT cached per orbit (region/model combo).
  - Authoring workflow: PR to policy repo => CI lint + unit tests => control plane publishes a policy bundle with a deterministic version id (policy_bundle:v{sha}).

2) Scoring model:
  - Each policy rule returns a small struct: {action, score_delta, confidence_hint, constraints_matched[]}. We avoid monolithic heuristics; scores are additive, with a base_score for each action and constraints contributing deltas.
  - Normalization: after aggregation, map raw_score into a [-1..1] or [0..100] range depending on downstream usage (routing probability vs hard prioritization). Keep the normalization function simple (sigmoid or linear clamp) so it's deterministic across runtimes.
  - Tie-breaking: stable deterministic tie-breaker using request_id hash + action_id to avoid nondeterministic flips across regions.

3) Inline vs async evaluation:
  - Fast-path: evaluate a compact subset of policy (precompiled predicates) inline in the serving runtime. Emit a compact attribution blob (<= 512 bytes) attached to the request trace. Keep the number of constraints evaluated under threshold (e.g., 16) via prefiltering indexes.
  - Deep-path: for complex bundles (newly published policies, heavy logic) route evaluation to control-plane policy-eval workers in-region. These return both decision and an explainability token used to fetch the full audit record asynchronously if needed.
content_4:
Explainability logging model:
- Two tiers of logs:
  1) Lightweight attribution (inline): small list of fired constraint ids + score deltas + policy_bundle_id + evaluation_time_ms. Stored as part of tracing (jaeger/span tag) and emitted to our frontline logs (hot path). Intended for quick triage and SLO dashboards.
  2) Audit record (async): full human-readable reason text, constraint evaluation traces, input context snapshot (redacted), diff against previous policy bundle, and links to test cases. Stored compressed in cold storage (S3 / GCS) and indexed into BigQuery/ES for queries.
- Privacy: never log raw PII. Walk through each context ref and apply per-field redaction policies, replace with deterministic hash if needed. Configurable field allowlist per customer/region.

Schema sketch for attribution blob (inline):
  - policy_bundle: string (sha)
content_5:
- fired: ["constraint_id:score_delta"] (short list)
  - decision_score: string (normalized number encoded as string to keep JSON flat)
  - eval_ms: string
  - explain_token: string (optional, opaque id to fetch audit record)

Storage & retention:
- Inline logs: 7d hot retention in logs system, then rollup records (1x per policy_bundle) persisted for 90d for cost-savvy dashboards.
- Audit records: 90d default, configurable to 1y for enterprise customers under contract. Cost center + quota applied.

Multi-region & control plane interactions:
- Policy bundles are published from control plane and signed. Each region pulls bundles on a short polling interval (e.g., 5s) and applies atomically. If a region has not pulled a newer bundle, it must include the bundle id in the response and the control plane will mark that region as "stale" for that bundle in the UI.
- Consistency mode flags per customer:
  - strong: refuse to route requests to region unless that region has active bundle vN (useful for regulatory constraints).
  - eventual: allow traffic, attach explainability token indicating possible divergence.
- Rollouts: canary bundles (10% traffic) handled by routing policy that includes stable hashing. Attribution must contain the rollout metadata so post-hoc queries can slice by canary cohort.

Operational playbook (short):
- Common alert: attribution_rate_spike (sudden increase in number of fired constraints) => check recent policy_bundle changes + CI results.
- Debug flow: use explain_token to retrieve audit record, correlate with trace id, and replay in a sandbox with older/newer bundles.

Performance considerations and optimizations:
- Precompile predicates to bytecode and keep ephemeral caches keyed by (bundle, region, model_variant).
- Use bloom filters for prefiltering constraints per-request to reduce evaluation set.
- Limit inline attribute size; offload full text reasons to async store.
- Telemetry sampling for heavy customers: capture 1% full audit records by default, higher for customers with SLA debugging enabled.
content_6:
Examples / micro-scenarios:
1) Routing for cost-sensitive workload:
  - Constraint A: customer_commit_tier == spot_eligible => score_delta = +20 for infer_low_cost_action
  - Constraint B: seq_len > 1024 => score_delta = -30 for infer_low_cost_action
  - If both fire, raw = base + (-10) => normalization -> prefer fallback to higher-capacity instance. Attribution blob shows B dominated decision.

2) Canary rollout mismatch (multi-region):
  - Canary is active in us-west only; a request routed to eu may evaluate older bundle and make a different decision. Inline attribution shows policy_bundle:oldsha and explain_token referencing audit record stored with region=europe. UI surfaces mismatch and suggests rerun with canary bundle for repro.

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Should we ship a lightweight DSL interpreter or depend on WASM for constraint execution? WASM buys polyglot but increases binary heft in runtime.
- How to balance deterministic tie-breakers versus randomness used for exploration experiments?
- Exact storage formats and field-level redaction list (per-compliance). Proposal: maintain a policy of minimal retention by default and allow opt-in extended retention.

Action items (next steps):
- Evan: prototype inline attribution blob (C++) and measure perf overhead on standard serving path (due 2024-10-02).
- Mateo: draft minimal DSL spec + examples and evaluate WASM vs precompiled bytecode (due 2024-10-09).
- Rina: define redaction whitelist + privacy checklist and run it against sample audit records (due 2024-09-27).
- Aisha: produce short RFC to product & compliance summarizing rollout modes and storage defaults (due 2024-10-15).

Notes / references:
- related GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/policy-eval/pull/402
- jira: PLATFORM-1243 (policy bundle lifecycle)
- internal confluence: https://confluence.internal/redwood/policy-eval-ops

Rough risk summary:
- Privacy: medium (must be conservative on input snapshots).
- Latency: low->medium depending on inline eval complexity and caching effectiveness.
- Operational complexity: medium (multi-region consistency + rollout plumbing adds complexity).

Footer: this doc is a working draft — expect changes as we experiment with precompilation and bundle rollout mechanics. Add comments inline or ping in #platform-policy for quick sync.
